description: Permissive CSV records, transductive row-world features and deterministic explained decision lists.
state: Raw UTF-8 CSV, header/rows, attribute/link world, known outcomes and ordered rules.
cost: For N rows, H columns and B bytes, splitting is O(B). read_world numeric sorting O(H*N log N); identifier branch recomputes an alphabetic count for every row O(H*N^2). Group expansion bounds groups to <=12, plus linear duplicate membership scans. Let A attributes and R rules: candidate generation O(R*N*sum_{j=1..min(k,3)} choose(A,j)) times BTreeMap comparison costs; rare learning stops at 14 and only enumerates up to pairs. run invokes repeated learners over 10 outer/inner folds and 15 settings. IO costs unmeasured.
forward: split_csv is a quote-toggle scanner: commas split only outside quotes, doubled quotes within quoted mode emit one quote, unmatched quotes are tolerated. read_csv removes blank physical lines, takes the first as header, and parses each remaining physical line independently. read_world selects name (>half), numeric (>=90% parseable and >12 distinct), category (<=12 distinct), or identifier paths in that order. learn_kc greedily chooses Laplace accuracy above majority+0.02 with support/min and cap; predict returns the first covering rule else default. run aligns test columns, builds joint train/test features, tunes folds and optionally writes output.
inverse: Behavior complement U minus scoped forward relation with dependencies fixed.
Reverse reconstruction retains all compatible antecedents; lossy fibers need not be singleton.
limitations: read_csv does not support quoted multiline records or validate width/quotes. run can panic on empty combined rows or malformed teacher/test indices, and output IDs are not CSV escaped. Numeric NaN may panic in partial_cmp unwrap. Features are inferred jointly on train/test, despite the old module prose claiming train-only. No live teacher, training corpus, file IO or CLI run is exercised.
Partial syntax projection; no semantic AST, broad accuracy claim or executable approximation.
